# Project terminal UI: per-repo base rows, header chips, project close dialog ## What to build The server already isolates project terminals: - **Create:** `POST /api/terminals { projectId, bases?: Record }` creates `.projects/

/.gm-worktrees/` with `repos/` linked to per-repo `gm-term/` worktrees. It answers `TerminalInfo` with `worktree: { id, path, branch, repos: [{ name, branch?, baseBranch?, isolated }] }` and optional `warnings`. - **Close:** `DELETE /api/terminals/:id` on a project terminal with work answers 409 `{ error, needsChoice: true, project: { dirty, ahead }, repos: [{ name, isolated, dirty, ahead }], branch, worktreeId }`. `?worktree=keep|delete` resolve it. - **Workspace dialog:** for workspaces, the New Terminal dialog already has a **Base** dropdown (from `GET /api/workspaces/:id/branches[?fetch=1]` → `{ branches, default, current?, fetched, error?, noCommit? }`), with a loading spinner and an offline note. This slice: 1. Adds `GET /api/projects/:id/branches` on the server. 2. Shows one **Base** row per repo when a project is selected in the dialog, and sends `bases`. 3. Shows per-repo chips in the pane header. 4. Shows a project version of the close dialog (per-repo work table; **Delete all / Keep all / Cancel**). The spec is `docs/prd/project-terminal-worktrees.md`. ## Context: files to read before implementing - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.tsx`: - `NewTerminalDialog` (~line 854 onward): it now contains the workspace **Base** field (testids `new-terminal-base`, `new-terminal-base-loading`, `new-terminal-base-offline`, `new-terminal-base-nocommit`). Mirror its fetch logic per repo. - `destroy` (~lines 278–312) and the `closing` state with `WorktreeCloseDialog` (~lines 713–733). - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/WorktreeClose.tsx` (74 lines) — `WorktreeWork`, `workText`, and `WorktreeCloseDialog` with testids `worktree-close`, `close-delete`, `close-keep`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/TerminalPane.tsx` (lines 215–240) — the `pane-branch` chip. - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/types.ts` (lines 73–106) — `TerminalInfo`, `BranchList`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/projects.ts` (lines 80–150) — project routes. Add the new route here. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runhome.ts` (lines 60–78) — `projectRepos` (repo name → workspace). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts` — the existing `GET /api/workspaces/:id/branches` handler. Extract its body into an exported helper (`branchInfo(ctx, ws, { fetch })`) and reuse it. - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.test.tsx` — `fetchMock` routes (~120–200); the close-dialog tests (~405–445); the existing Base-field tests. ## Patterns to follow **Server route** — like the other project routes: ```ts app.get<{ Params: { id: string } }>("/api/projects/:id/branches", async (req, reply) => { const project = ctx.store.project(req.params.id); if (!project) return reply.code(404).send({ error: "project not found" }); … }); ``` **Close dialog** — build a `ProjectWorktreeCloseDialog` next to `WorktreeCloseDialog` in `WorktreeClose.tsx`, with the same `createPortal`, `useFocusTrap` and `dialog-overlay` structure. Keep the testids `worktree-close`, `close-delete` (label "Delete all") and `close-keep` (label "Keep all"), and add `close-work-table`. ## Step-by-step tasks ### ADD `GET /api/projects/:id/branches` in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/projects.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `{ repos: [{ name, workspaceId, branches, default, current?, noCommit? }] }` from local refs only (no fetch), one entry per repo of `project.json`, in order. Use `projectRepos` and the extracted branch helper. A repo without a workspace → `{ name, branches: [], missing: true }`. Unknown project → 404. - **VALIDATE**: a test in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/projects.test.ts`: two committed repos → two entries with `default: "main"`; an uncommitted repo → `noCommit: true`. ### UPDATE `NewTerminalDialog` in `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.tsx` - **IMPLEMENT**: when a project option is selected: 1. `GET /api/projects//branches` and render one row per repo: `
